# DEM reference fixtures

`gdal-n43.tif` is an unchanged copy of [OSGeo/GDAL v3.11.4, autotest/gdrivers/data/n43.tif](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/v3.11.4/autotest/gdrivers/data/n43.tif), retrieved on 2026-09-27. It is a 121 × 121 Int16, LZW, PixelIsPoint WGS 84 DEM. The upstream license is retained in `GDAL-LICENSE.txt`. `manifest.json` records its SHA-256 and samples independently decoded with tifffile/imagecodecs. This is an independent GIS fixture, not an OpenTopography API response.

The remaining files were generated by `../generate_fixtures.py` with tifffile 2026.9.20, imagecodecs 2026.8.16 and NumPy 2.5.3. They exercise little/big endian, strip boundaries, lossless codecs and predictors, tiled BigTIFF, signed/unsigned/floating-point samples, NoData and explicit rejection paths. The writer is independent of the Bmaps C wrapper. These synthetic fixtures are not evidence of all provider output variants.

Regeneration requires those Python packages in a temporary virtual environment. Run the generator from any working directory. Check in the regenerated files and manifest together. `DemFixtureBytes.kt` contains exact Base64 copies of `int16-be-lzw.tif` and `float32-tiled-bigtiff.tif` for portable Android/iOS smoke tests; refresh those copies if the fixtures change. Runtime tests require no Python or network access.

`../generate_large_fixture.py /tmp/bmaps-dem-large.tif` generates a sparse, uncompressed, 512 MiB BigTIFF raster outside the repository, with known samples at the start, middle and end. The native harness supports `dem_test --large /tmp/bmaps-dem-large.tif`. This checks random access without committing a large binary or allocating the full raster during generation.
